title: The Invention of the Folding Wheelchair
summary: How Herbert Everest and Harry Jennings built a light, folding wheelchair in 1932 that became the model for most modern wheelchairs, helping people move independently.
poll: The folding wheelchair is one of the most important inventions for giving people independence.

versions.title: A Chair With Wheels
versions.text:
See that chair with big wheels. It is a wheelchair. It helps a person move.

Some people cannot walk well. A chair like this helps them. It helps them go places on their own.

Long ago, these chairs were heavy. They were made of wood. They did not fold up. They were hard to carry.

In 1932, two men made a new kind. One man, Everest, got hurt in a mine. He used a chair like this each day. His friend, Jennings, liked to build things.

The two men made a chair. It could fold flat. It was made of light metal, not wood. It was easy to carry. It could fit in a car.

This new chair became a model. Many other chairs copied it.

Now, chairs like this help many people. Kids use them to get to school. Adults use them to get to work. Some people use them to play sports.

Some chairs have a small motor. You push a button and it moves. Other chairs you push with your hands.

Chairs like this give people freedom. They help people go where they want.

versions.title: A Chair With Wheels
versions.text:
A wheelchair is a chair that has wheels on it. It helps people move from place to place. Some people have trouble walking. A chair like this lets them get around on their own.

Long ago, these chairs were heavy. They were made of wood. They were hard to fold or carry.

In 1932, two men in America made a new kind. One man, Everest, got hurt in a mine. He used a chair like this every day. His friend, Jennings, liked to build things. Jennings was good with machines.

Together, they made a chair that could fold flat. It was made of light metal. It was not wood. It was easy to carry. It could fit in a car.

This new kind became a model. Most wheelchairs still copy it today.

Chairs like this now help millions of people. Kids use them to go to school. Adults use them to go to work. Many people play sports, like wheelchair basketball.

Some wheelchairs have a small motor. A person pushes a button, and the chair moves. Other chairs are pushed along by hand.

Wheelchairs give people real freedom. They let people go where they want.

versions.title: A Chair With Wheels
versions.text:
A wheelchair is a chair built with wheels. It lets a person sit and move at the same time. It helps people who cannot walk well get from place to place.

Long ago, these chairs were heavy. They were made of wood. They were hard to fold up or carry anywhere.

In 1932, two men in America changed this. One man, Everest, had been hurt in a mining accident. He used a chair like this every day. His friend, Jennings, was a clever engineer. He liked to build new things.

Together, the two friends made a chair. It could fold flat in seconds. It was built from light metal, not heavy wood. This made it much easier to carry.

This folding design became the model most wheelchairs follow today, ninety years later.

Wheelchairs now help millions of people. People use them to go to school, to go to work, and to play sports like wheelchair basketball.

Some wheelchairs today have a small motor. A person can push a button, and it moves by itself. Other chairs are pushed along by hand.

Wheelchairs give people real freedom. They let people choose where to go.

versions.title: The Wheelchair That Could Fold
versions.text:
A wheelchair is a chair fitted with wheels. It lets a person sit and move without needing to stand or walk. For many people, it is simply the tool that makes daily life possible.

Chairs with wheels have existed for hundreds of years. Early versions were heavy. They were built from solid wood. They were hard to fold or carry.

That changed in 1932. Two men in the United States built a very different wheelchair. Everest had been hurt in a mining accident. He used a wheelchair every day and knew its flaws firsthand. His friend Jennings, a skilled engineer, wanted to design something better.

Working together, Everest and Jennings made a wheelchair that could fold flat within seconds. It was built from light metal, not heavy wood. It was much easier to carry.

That folding design became the plan that wheelchairs still follow, ninety years later.

Today, wheelchairs help millions of people lead full lives. People use wheelchairs to attend school, hold jobs, travel, and compete in sports such as wheelchair basketball.

Many wheelchairs now include a small motor. A rider presses a button, and the chair moves with no pushing needed. Other wheelchairs stay manual, pushed by hand.

More than anything, a wheelchair means freedom: choosing where to go and what to do next.

versions.title: The Wheelchair That Could Fold
versions.text:

Everything changed in 1932, when two men in the United States built a strikingly different wheelchair. Everest, who had been seriously hurt in a mining accident, relied on a wheelchair daily. He understood its flaws firsthand. His friend Jennings, a skilled engineer, was determined to design something better.

Working closely, Everest and Jennings made a wheelchair that could fold completely flat in only seconds. Built from light metal instead of heavy wood, it was much easier to carry and to store.

That folding design eventually became the plan that most wheelchairs still follow today, ninety years later.

Today, wheelchairs help millions of people lead full lives. People rely on wheelchairs to attend school, hold demanding jobs, travel, and compete in sports such as wheelchair basketball.

Many wheelchairs now include a small built-in motor. A rider presses a button, and the chair rolls forward with no pushing at all. Other wheelchairs remain manual, pushed by hand.

More than anything else, a wheelchair represents real freedom: the simple ability to choose where to go and what to do next.

versions.title: The Invention of the Folding Wheelchair
versions.text:
A wheelchair is a mobility device fitted with wheels. It is engineered so a user can sit and travel between locations without needing to stand or walk unaided. For countless people, it is the everyday tool that makes independent living possible.

Chairs fitted with wheels have existed for hundreds of years across many cultures, from ancient China to medieval Europe. Early records depict wheeled seating for people with limited mobility. Those early versions, though, were cumbersome. They were built almost entirely from solid wood, and nearly impossible to fold or transport.

Everything changed in 1932, when two men in the United States engineered a strikingly different kind of wheelchair. Herbert Everest, who had been seriously injured in a mining accident, relied on a wheelchair daily and understood its shortcomings firsthand. His friend Harry Jennings, a skilled mechanical engineer, wanted to design something more practical.

Collaborating closely, Everest and Jennings created a wheelchair capable of folding completely flat within seconds, a revolutionary feature at the time. It was built from lightweight tubular steel rather than heavy wood. It proved much easier to carry and to store.

That folding design ultimately became the blueprint that most modern wheelchairs continue to follow, even today, shaping models from hospitals to competitive racing.

Today, wheelchairs help millions of people lead full, independent lives. People depend on them to attend school, hold careers, travel, and compete in sports such as wheelchair basketball and wheelchair racing.

Many wheelchairs now include a small built-in electric motor, letting a rider press a button so the chair glides forward with no pushing required. Other wheelchairs remain manual, propelled by hand using the two large wheels mounted along each side.

Whichever kind a person uses, the basic idea stays the same: a wheelchair should fit the user's life, rather than forcing the user to fit around its limits.

MID.modelAnswer: Herbert Everest had been injured in a mining accident and relied on a wheelchair every day, so he understood its flaws firsthand. Together with his friend Harry Jennings, a skilled mechanical engineer, he set out in 1932 to design something better. The two built a wheelchair made of lightweight metal tubing that could fold completely flat within seconds, unlike the heavy wooden wheelchairs of the time. This made it far easier to carry, store, and fit into a car. Their folding design became the basic blueprint that most modern wheelchairs still follow today, helping millions of people live independent, active lives.

HIGH.modelAnswer: For centuries, wheeled chairs existed in various cultures, but they remained cumbersome, built almost entirely from solid wood, and nearly impossible to fold or transport with any practicality, which confined their usefulness to a single home. In 1932, Herbert Everest, who relied on a wheelchair daily after a mining accident, collaborated closely with his friend Harry Jennings, a skilled mechanical engineer, to address these shortcomings directly. Over many months, the two men tested prototype after prototype until they achieved a design capable of folding completely flat within seconds, built from lightweight tubular steel rather than heavy wood. This combination of portability and durability meant a wheelchair user could, for the first time, travel almost anywhere a car could go. As a result, their design became the fundamental blueprint that most modern wheelchairs continue to follow, enabling millions of people worldwide to attend school, pursue careers, and compete in elite sports entirely on their own terms.
